chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one among you who stretches out his neck the most in this world will be the one who hungers the most on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.أَطْوَلَكُمْ: The one who is longest / most extended
key_terms.جُشَاءً: Stretching out the neck (an idiom for eating greedily or excessively)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of overeating in this world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on sacrifices and foods, this hadith links physical consumption to spiritual accountability, emphasizing that gluttony in the dunya results in prolonged hunger on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a foundational ethical principle in Shia jurisprudence, urging believers to view dietary moderation not merely as health advice but as a means of preparing the soul for the afterlife.
